questions.q: What is a lock, in SQL Server terms?
options: A flag recording that a transaction holds a claim on a resource, tracked by the lock manager
A password required to open a database connection
A setting that disables all queries on a table
A backup of a row taken before it is modified
questions.explain: The lock manager tracks who holds what kind of lock on which resource so other transactions know whether they can proceed.

questions.q: Which ACID property (Lesson 101) does locking exist to enforce?
options: Isolation
Atomicity
Durability
Consistency only, never Isolation
questions.explain: Locking is the mechanism that keeps concurrent transactions from seeing each other's incomplete, in-progress work.

questions.q: In the two-session scenario, why does Session B's SELECT against ProductID 680 block?
options: Session A holds an exclusive lock on that row until it commits or rolls back, and Session B's read request conflicts with it
SQL Server always blocks every SELECT statement by default
Session B's query has a syntax error
AdventureWorks2012 locks the entire database during any write
questions.explain: Session A's open UPDATE transaction holds the lock; Session B must wait until Session A commits or rolls back.

questions.q: What makes Session B's blocked query finally return?
options: Session A running COMMIT TRANSACTION or ROLLBACK TRANSACTION
Restarting the SQL Server service
Session B retyping the same SELECT statement
Waiting exactly 30 seconds, regardless of Session A's state
questions.explain: Once Session A ends its transaction one way or the other, the lock is released and Session B's request can be granted.

questions.q: Why can't locking simply be turned off in SQL Server?
options: Without it, Isolation and Consistency couldn't be enforced — readers could see half-committed writes and writers could overwrite each other
It can be turned off, and most production systems do
Locking is only used for backups, not for normal queries
Turning it off would only affect DDL statements like ALTER TABLE
questions.explain: Locking is the mechanism behind two of the four ACID properties, not an optional performance feature — isolation levels only adjust how much of it applies, never remove it.
